item.text: {"text":"The [original BERT4Rec paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690) trains by predicting original item IDs at masked positions, adds last-item-only masking examples, and appends [MASK] at inference. The official runnable generator, [gen_data_fin.py](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py), forms sliding windows, creates dupe_factor differently corrupted copies per window, then adds one last-item-only example per window. force_last=True instead selects each user’s final window and masks its final eligible position. Random masking selects min(max_predictions_per_seq, max(1, round(length × masked_lm_prob))) positions without replacement. Crucially, masked_lm_prob controls target selection; mask_prob controls replacement conditional on selection: [MASK] with probability p, unchanged with (1−p)/2, random catalog item with (1−p)/2. Labels always retain original IDs. Despite 80/10/10 comments, the [official MovieLens script](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run_ml-1m.sh) sets mask_prob=1.0, masked_lm_prob=0.2, dupe_factor=10: all selected targets become [MASK].\n\nInterpretation for leakage: the generator corrupts positions, leaving genuine repeated-item occurrences elsewhere untouched; random replacement can also coincidentally equal the target. These differ from exposing shifted targets through bidirectional inputs, which the paper explicitly identifies as leakage. Unchanged selected targets are an optional corruption branch, absent when mask_prob=1.0. For a precise proposed α ablation, define α as the probability of choosing a last-item-only training example versus random-position masking; keep corruption probability, mask proportion, window sampling, and loss normalization fixed. With ten random copies plus one last-only copy per window, the official generator’s last-only example fraction is 1/11, although its target-level loss contribution depends on reduction. This α definition is a proposed experimental choice, not a published parameter."}
